newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran leader says forced marriages un-Islamic.
newsitem.headline: Iran leader says forced marriages un-Islamic.

text.p: Iran's supreme leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei on Monday blasted as un-Islamic the practice of forcing girls to marry against their will, state-run Tehran radio said.

"Imposing marriage on girls ... is among principles opposed by (Islamic) sharia law, and traditions such as this have nothing to do with Islam and should be corrected," Khamenei was quoted as telling a gathering of women in Iran's southwestern Khuzestan province.
Khamenei was speaking about ... "pagan tradition, practiced in certain parts of the country and in some Moslem states, which are contradictory to explicit Islamic rulings", the radio said.
He was apparently referring to practices in some communities, including among Khuzestan's ethnic Arab tribes, of marrying off daughters against their will, sometimes to much older men.
Iranian leaders have in the past few years repeatedly warned local clans to desist from practices which flaunt national laws.
During the 1980-88 Iran-Iraq war Tehran's Islamic leaders courted the tightly-knit, armed Arab clans whose loyalty was essential in the sensitive oil regions on the Iraqi border.
But press reports of practices, such as relatives killing women accused of immoral acts, have led to calls for ending the tribes' defiance of national legal authorities.
